#### List:

- Intro
- Type 1 reaction
- Type 4 reaction

#### Intro:

+--------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Definition   | - Hypersensitivity to latex a natural derivative of the rubber tree |
+--------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Risk factors | - Atopy (asthma, eczema, allergic rhinitis)                         |
|              | - Frequent exposure (i.e. health care workers)                      |
+--------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Severity     | - Varies from mild to life-threatening                              |
+--------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Source       | - Hospitals: disposable gloves, urine catheters, anaesthetic tubing |
|              | - Anywhere: rubber bands, shoes                                     |
|              | - Cross-sensitivity: banana, kiwifruit, avocado                     |
+--------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Implication  | - Minimise exposure: stock latex-only gloves and other products     |
+--------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Type 1: anaphylaxis

+-----------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Characteristics | - All-or-nothing                                                              |
|                 | - Immediate                                                                   |
|                 | - Life-threatening                                                            |
+-----------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Aetiology       | - First exposure → sensitization (10-14 days)                                 |
|                 |   - Antigen presenting cell engulfs antigen, presents on MHC-II               |
|                 |   - APC activates specific T cell                                             |
|                 |   - T cell activates specific B cell                                          |
|                 |   - B cell produces specific IgE                                              |
|                 |   - IgE fixes to mast cells and basophils                                     |
|                 |   - 10-14 day process                                                         |
|                 | - Second exposure → systemic degranulation (seconds)                          |
+-----------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Pathophysiology | - Early mediators: histamine, serotonin, tryptase                             |
|                 | - Late mediators: leukotrienes, prostaglandins, bradykinin, platelet factor 4 |
|                 | - Vasodilation, capillary leak                                                |
|                 | - Angioedema, upper airway obstruction                                        |
|                 | - Hypotension, arrest                                                         |
|                 | - Bronchospasm                                                                |
+-----------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Treatment       | - Adrenaline                                                                  |
|                 |   - α~1~: vasoconstriction → ↑SVR → ↑mAP                                      |
|                 |   - β~1~: ↑heart rate, contractility → ↑mAP                                   |
|                 |   - β~2~: bronchodilatation, stabilize mast cells                             |
|                 | - Glucocorticoid:                                                             |
|                 |   - ↓Late mediator production                                                 |
|                 |   - Antihistamine                                                             |
|                 |   - ↓Vasodilation, capillary leak                                             |
+-----------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Test            | - Prick skin →apply latex solution → observe for weal and flare               |
|                 | - Radioallergosorbent assay                                                   |
|                 | - Serial tryptase (+1h, +6h)                                                  |
+-----------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Type 4: delayed type hypersensitivity, contact dermatitis

+-----------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Key features                | - Slower                                                            |
|                             | - Generally less severe                                             |
+-----------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Aetiology / pathophysiology | - Antigen presented to T lymphocyte                                 |
|                             | - Cytokine release                                                  |
|                             | - Local activation of macrophages                                   |
|                             | - Well demarcated erythematous urticarial rash                      |
+-----------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Test                        | - Apply skin patch with antigen for 24 hours → observe for reaction |
+-----------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
